issue.title: gateway: fast JSON marshal parity tests fail on Go 1.27.3 (raw separators and invalid UTF-8)
issue.body:
On unchanged upstream `435f0415140ca58a8af49eab46754d4903d35da9`, macOS arm64 / Go 1.27.3, these existing tests fail reproducibly under a temporary HOME with GOPATH/GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE pinned:

```sh
go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway -run '^Test(MarshalRawIsEncodingJSON|MarshalSizedIsJSONMarshal)$' -count=1
```

- `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON`, `fastjson_marshal_test.go:64`: with HTML escaping disabled, `marshalRaw` leaves U+2028/U+2029 literal in a raw JSON string, while this runtime's `encoding/json` emits escapes. the raw-value appender in `fastjson.go` gates those escapes on `escapeHTML`.
- `TestMarshalSizedIsJSONMarshal`, `long_turn_copies_test.go:84-87`: the custom writer emits invalid UTF-8 replacements as six-byte `\ufffd` escapes, while this runtime's `json.Marshal` emits the UTF-8 replacement character. The computed size consequently differs (1055 vs 671 for the all-byte fixture). See the string size/writer helpers in `fastjson.go`.

Found during GLM auto-reset contribution validation, then reproduced in a detached clean worktree at the exact upstream commit above. No auto-reset changes are present in that reproduction. This reports the byte/size contract mismatch; it does not claim invalid JSON or that Go itself is at fault. The custom encoding and its size calculation should be reconciled with the supported runtime contract. No fix is included in the unrelated feature patch.

comments.body:
Fixed on [fix/5348-json-runtime-parity](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5348-json-runtime-parity), commit [102f2b1d](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/102f2b1de6d718d62f0ae8fa53fd6ca469ecff50), based on upstream `ed0ab567`.

The fast encoder now derives the separator and invalid-UTF-8 replacement behavior once from the active `encoding/json` implementation. The string writer and size calculation use the same replacement bytes. HTML escaping remains separately controlled, and the existing fast path is retained. This avoids hard-coding Go 1.27 behavior into builds using the supported Go 1.26.8 runtime.

On the unchanged base, the two reported tests fail on Go 1.27.3 and pass on cached Go 1.26.8. After the patch, focused exact-byte and size parity tests pass on both. Independent review also ran all 29 existing fuzz seeds and a real Responses-to-Chat Handler test under race detection; nogui vet/build pass. Existing equality assertions were not relaxed.

No full repository suite, native macOS/Windows run or performance benchmark was performed. The linked fork PRs were checked: they cite these failures as pre-existing and do not change the encoder. AI-assisted implementation and independent review.

issue.title: provider: opt-in GLM API-key auto-reset on quota exhaustion (scoped patch + live API evidence)

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
This delivers a small, provider-key-only auto-reset patch for #2568 and #2716, with a fresh live check of BigModel's API-key authentication. Thanks to @Jichao for the endpoint investigation in #2716; the commit credits that contribution.

### Live evidence (2026-11-05)

Using the personal GLM Coding Plan API key already configured in Magpie, without a ZCode or browser session:

- `GET https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/biz/customer-package-reset/list?targetType=PERSONAL` returned available weekly cards.
- `POST /api/biz/customer-package-reset/use`, with the bare API key in `Authorization` and `{targetType: "PERSONAL", resetType: "WEEK", recordId: <selected ID>, grantType: "GLOBAL", requestId: <UUID>}`, returned `code: 200, success: true`.
- A separate quota read changed five-hour usage **100% → 0%** and weekly usage **69% → 0%**. Available weekly cards changed **3 → 2**.

This was an explicitly authorized manual API call. It verifies the vendor protocol and weekly-card behavior; it is not a live test of the new automatic gateway path. No account IDs, keys or sessions are included here. Z.ai has not been live-tested by this contribution.

### Proposed behavior and patch scope

`magpie provider auto-reset <id> on|off` opts one personal GLM plan key into automatic consumption. Default: off. It follows the exact key and vendor; replacing a key does not inherit consent. The initial command enables single-key providers; disabling remains possible after adding another key.

After every candidate is unavailable and a request receives a quota-exhaustion refusal, the gateway re-reads personal quota, chooses the matching unexpired card with the earliest expiry, consumes it, verifies quota recovery and retries the request. Weekly exhaustion takes priority. A five-hour exhaustion does not automatically spend a more valuable weekly card if no five-hour card exists.

A separate per-key, machine-local state file and cross-process lock protect consumption. The original window deadline, selected record and request ID are written atomically **before** the POST. Uncertain responses, failed writes/reads/locks and restarts cannot turn into another automatic POST during that window. Toggling off/on preserves the reservation. Codex's state and history remain separate.

This patch covers API-key providers. ZCode plugin accounts, team cards, expiry scheduling, peak-hour policy and a GUI settings switch are outside this first patch. The routing story identifies GLM in all supported translations. Automated consumption should be enabled on only one machine for a given key.

### Delivery and verification

Draft PR on my fork: https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/pull/2

Commit: https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie/commit/8ab06857d82695bcdb077ace24b558a74c7519f2

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/hhh2210/magpie.git feat/glm-key-auto-reset
git cherry-pick 8ab06857d82695bcdb077ace24b558a74c7519f2
```

Based on upstream `435f04151`. Diff: production **+266/-2**, tests **+288/-0**, docs **+39/-0**.

Passed:
- Focused provider, CLI and gateway tests; provider/gateway `-race -count=3` (sandbox HOME/config, pinned Go caches).
- Behavioral regression: disabling the new gateway integration makes `TestGLMAutoResetRequest` fail with HTTP 429 / zero spends / one attempt; restoring it gives HTTP 200 / one spend / successful retry.
- Native, Linux and Windows vet/build; built CLI on/off under synthetic configuration; formatting/diff checks.
- Headless Chromium routing-story checks in English and Chinese, including GLM text. Full provider and CLI packages pass.

Not green / not run:
- Full `go test -tags nogui ./...`: JSON marshal parity failures (#5348, reproduced on unchanged base), gateway package exceeded its 10-minute budget, `TestLaneLimitRoutes` (#5150), `TestPluginSOCKSProxy` (#2207; existing fix branch is tracked there).
- `i18n-keys`: existing #5332 failure (`View routing` in a Go-test comment).
- WebKit, full browser suite and live automatic spending not run. Environment: macOS arm64, Go 1.27.3, Bun 1.4.4.

No production Magpie binary or auto-reset setting was changed.

The live automatic-spend gate requested in #2716 remains open. Please treat this as a **draft for review**, not a claim that all merge gates passed. A real card was already used for the protocol check; no further cards were spent just to generate test evidence.

For integration, please cherry-pick the linked commit with its author retained. If squashing or reimplementing the patch, please preserve `Co-authored-by: hhh2210 <hzy2210@gmail.com>` and the contribution credit already in the commit.

issue.title: [功能建议] 将“资源库 → 子代理”改为“代理”，支持设置为主代理或子代理

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 需求

希望将“资源库 → 子代理”统一改为“资源库 → 代理”，并在新增、编辑代理时，支持设置该代理作为**主代理**或**子代理**使用。

## 使用场景

自定义代理除了被其他代理调用，也可以作为用户直接对话、发起任务的主代理。希望在资源库中统一管理这些代理，并明确它们的使用角色。

## 期望行为

- 资源库入口及相关页面名称由“子代理”改为“代理”。
- 新增、编辑代理时，可以选择“主代理”或“子代理”。
- 同步到目标客户端时，在客户端支持的范围内，让代理按所选角色生效：主代理可作为用户直接使用的会话入口，子代理可供其他代理调用。
- 对于不支持某种角色的客户端，在界面中明确说明支持范围。
- 已有子代理保留原有配置和用途，升级后默认仍为子代理。

核心是让资源库统一管理代理，并显式设置其角色。具体界面与各客户端的适配方式可由维护者决定。

issue.title: Library: installing a skill from a SHA-256 git repository fails with `mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256`

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
# Library: installing a skill from a SHA-256 git repository fails with `mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256`

## What happens

Adding a skill from a git repository that uses SHA-256 object format fails before anything is fetched:

```
fatal: mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256
```

Magpie shows it as:

```
git couldn't fetch https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git: fatal: mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256
```

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.3038, macOS 27.0.1, arm64
- `/opt/homebrew/bin/git` 2.56.0 and Apple Git-2.54 (`/usr/bin/git`) both support SHA-256 repositories

## Steps to reproduce

1. `https://gitea.com/gitea/cli` is a SHA-256 repository (every ref from `git ls-remote` is a 64-char hash).
2. In Library, add a skill from `https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/src/branch/main/skills/gt` (or the clone URL `https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git`).
3. Magpie fails with the error above.

## It is not the user's git

Both installed git versions clone the repository fine in a terminal:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git
```

The failure comes from the sequence Magpie runs itself.

## Cause

`internal/library/skillgit.go`, `fetchGit()`:

```go
if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "init", "-q"); err != nil {
    return fail(err)
}
...
if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", "--no-tags", "--", src.Repo, ref); err != nil {
```

`git init` creates a **SHA-1** repository (the client default), while the remote is **SHA-256**. Git refuses the fetch instead of converting, so every SHA-256 host is unreachable, regardless of the git version.

Reproduced with plain git:

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
git init -q
git fetch --depth 1 --no-tags -- https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git main
# fatal: mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256
```

The same fetch succeeds when the local repository is SHA-256:

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
GIT_DEFAULT_HASH=sha256 git init -q
git fetch --depth 1 --no-tags -- https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git main
git rev-parse --show-object-format   # sha256
```

## Suggested fix

### Option A: let `git clone` negotiate the format

Replace the manual `init` + `fetch` with:

```go
git clone --depth 1 --no-tags -c protocol.ext.allow=never -c core.symlinks=false -- <repo> <tmp>
```

`git clone` reads the remote's `object-format` capability and creates a matching repository, so SHA-1 and SHA-256 hosts both work with no probing. (The existing shallow-fetch fallback for dumb HTTP would still need to be kept.)

### Option B: retry as SHA-256 on that specific error

Keep the current flow, but if the fetch fails with `mismatched algorithms`, recreate the temp repository with the remote's format and retry:

```go
if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", "--no-tags", "--", src.Repo, ref); err != nil {
    if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(err.Error()), "mismatched algorithms") {
        if err := os.RemoveAll(tmp); err != nil {
            return fail(err)
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o700); err != nil {
            return fail(err)
        }
        if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "init", "-q", "--object-format=sha256"); err != nil {
            return fail(err)
        }
        if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", "--no-tags", "--", src.Repo, ref); err != nil {
            return fail(err)
        }
    } else if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(err.Error()), "shallow") {
        return fail(err)
    } else if _, err := runGit(ctx, git, env, tmp, src, "fetch", "-q", "--no-tags", "--", src.Repo, ref); err != nil {
        return fail(err)
    }
}
```

`--object-format=sha256` needs git >= 2.29; on older git the retry fails and the original error is still the useful one, so this can be treated as best-effort.

### Related: `hexRef` rejects 64-char hashes

```go
hexRef = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}$`)
```

SHA-256 repositories report 64-char commit ids. `gitRemoteHead()` maps `ls-remote` output through `hexRef`, so for a SHA-256 remote every value is rejected and the head comes back empty (affects update checks, and pinning a skill to a full SHA-256 commit). It should accept up to 64 hex chars.

## Workaround for users

Until this is fixed, mirror the skill into a SHA-1 repository and install from a `file://` URL:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://gitea.com/gitea/cli.git /tmp/gitea-cli
mkdir -p ~/mirrors/gt-skill
cp -R /tmp/gitea-cli/skills/gt/. ~/mirrors/gt-skill/
cd ~/mirrors/gt-skill
git init -q -b main
git add -A
git -c user.name=mirror -c user.email=mirror@localhost commit -qm "gt skill"
```

Then add `file:///Users/<you>/mirrors/gt-skill` in Library.

issue.title: usage: make allowance charts selectable and card widths adjustable

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
> **Fork review draft:** This PR targets `goubo/magpie`, not `yetone/magpie`. Upstream restricts PR creation to collaborators; GitHub rejected this account's upstream `CreatePullRequest` request. The same branch is available for upstream review at https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...goubo:codex/quota-chart-selection .

## Problem and behavior

Allowance cards currently combine every quota window on one time axis. A five-hour window beside a weekly or monthly window becomes difficult to inspect, and the 260px card minimum leaves little room for long plan names and multiple series. This change lets the reader choose the windows to compare, switch their horizontal alignment, and adjust the overview's card width locally.

### Allowance charts

- Turn the existing legend into multi-select buttons. Initially all windows are selected; only selected windows determine the plotted curves, time range, pace references and pace text. Colors and colorblind patterns keep their original series identity. Deselecting every window leaves the legend available to restore them.
- Add **Use actual time**, on by default. On, selected windows share the real time axis and retain their per-window pace references. Off, each window's complete recorded cycle fills the chart width, with one common full-to-empty diagonal reference and Cycle start / Cycle end labels. Horizontal positions in this mode represent cycle progress; they do not mean that samples occurred at the same timestamp. Sample readings still show their actual times and values.
- Hide the switch when fewer than two legend entries are available, and render actual time in that case. Selecting one of several available entries keeps the switch available. A temporarily hidden switch retains its saved multi-window preference.
- Keep compact charts free of extra ticks and sample readouts. Expanded charts provide percentage labels and exact recorded samples through pointer, touch and keyboard input. Refreshing retains the expanded state within the page.
- Preserve historical snapshot ownership and meters, two-day actual-time behavior, reset gaps and tray/balance calculations. Cycle-progress mode uses the complete recorded cycle even when the global range is two days; switching back restores that actual-time range. A cycle without usable start/reset bounds is omitted with an explanation rather than assigned an invented range.

### Overview layout

- Add a **Layout** popover to the Allowances heading, using the app's existing menu placement and focus behavior.
- Change the default minimum card width from **260px to 360px**. Offer a **280–560px slider in 20px steps**, plus Compact (280), Comfortable (360) and Spacious (440) presets, live preview and the actual column/card-width readout.
- Use the same minimum in the CSS fallback and the JavaScript packer. A container narrower than the preference uses one fitting column; long plan names wrap inside the card. Keep packing order, bottom alignment, chart choices and reading position.
- Handle cold lazy imports without replacing a menu opened later or stealing its focus, and clean up popover observers/listeners when it closes.

## Scope, state and compatibility

The affected subsystem is the [GUI app shell](docs/subsystems/gui-shell.md). Implementation is in [app.js](internal/gui/assets/app.js), [quotacurve.js](internal/gui/assets/quotacurve.js), the [Usage page](internal/gui/assets/plugins/usage/page.js) and its [layout module](internal/gui/assets/plugins/usage/layout.js), with scoped CSS, five-language strings, browser tests and subsystem documentation. The chart interaction and layout controls load lazily to stay within the existing core-script budget; loading the chart module invalidates the packing cache so its final height is measured.

Presentation preferences use existing browser-local storage conventions:

| Key | Value and default |
| --- | --- |
| `magpie.quotaCurveHidden` | Per-account hidden window names, keyed by provider plus normalized account name; absent means all visible. |
| `magpie.quotaCurveRelative` | Accounts using cycle-progress alignment; absent means actual time. |
| `magpie.usageCardMinWidth` | Numeric minimum in pixels; absent/invalid uses 360. Opening the popover alone does not rewrite an invalid stored value. Width changes synchronize between windows. |

There is no server-side preference migration or new dependency. Backend APIs, quota calculation, provider polling, gateway routing, history storage and the database are unchanged. The shared expanded-curve behavior also serves balance charts, so balance and sample-readout regressions are included below.

The larger default can reduce the number of columns and increase page height; the Compact preset provides a denser layout. This is a product layout change and needs maintainer acceptance before merge. All preferences are local to the browser/profile. This PR does not merge, deploy or replace an installed magpie.

## Verification

Tested head: `1a5b0d7803933c772436b526ef7f6a983ae52e17`, rebased on `2f660ca86b1511c624101003fdf66da6ef2c9036`. Tests ran on macOS arm64 with Go 1.27.3 and existing dependencies. Go checks use an isolated temporary HOME, clear agent/MAGPIE/XDG environment overrides, and pin the existing `GOPATH`, `GOMODCACHE` and `GOCACHE`. Browser tests use local fixtures rather than vendor APIs. Linux/Windows results are cross-vet/build checks, not native runtime tests.

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| 15 relevant browser test files, Chromium + WebKit, five languages, narrow/wide layouts | **237/237 passed**, exit 0. Command below. |
| `node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-concurrency=2 internal/gui/tests/{quota-read-at,balance-curve,balance-currencies}.test.cjs` | **14/14 passed**, exit 0, both engines. |
| `go test -p 2 -tags nogui ./internal/gui -run 'TestCoreScriptBudget\|TestDatesFollowGUILanguage\|TestPurposeAssetMatchesUsage' -count=1 -timeout 5m` | Passed, exit 0; budget was not increased. |
| `go vet -p 2 ./...` | Passed, exit 0, macOS. |
| `GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet -p 2 -tags nogui ./...` | Passed, exit 0. |
| `GOOS=windows CGO_ENABLED=0 go vet -p 2 ./...` | Passed, exit 0. |
| `go build -p 2 -o <temporary-output> .` | Passed, exit 0; SDK deprecation/linker warnings remain. |
| `GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -p 2 -tags nogui -o <temporary-output> .` | Passed, exit 0. |
| `GOOS=windows CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -p 2 -o <temporary-output> .` | Passed, exit 0. |
| `go test -p 2 -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...` | **Failed, exit 1**: 84 packages passed and 3 failed (`internal/agent`, `internal/gateway`, `internal/gui`). Exact failed tests and issue references below. |
| `node --test internal/gui/tests/{i18n-en-no-cjk,i18n-keys}.test.cjs` | **7/8 passed**, exit 1. The failing `a plugin's words are its own` assertion reports the three conflicts listed below. |
| `node --check` on all 13 changed JS/CJS files; `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` | Passed, each exit 0. |
| `gofmt -l` on changed Go files | Not applicable: no Go source changed. |
| Entire GUI suite | **Not run**; the selected files exercise the affected chart, packing, menu, refresh and header paths. Full GUI acceptance remains outstanding before merge. |
| Native Linux/Windows GUI/runtime | **Not run**. |
| GitHub CI | No workflow run or status check was present for this fork branch when inspected; no CI pass is claimed. |
| Native source GUI preview | Previously inspected against the local installed backend from an isolated test configuration. The test GUI has exited and its port has no listener; the installed application was left running. No private account screenshots or logs are uploaded. |

Relevant browser command (using the already installed Playwright runtime):

```sh
node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-concurrency=2 \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-card-width.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-pack.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-arrange.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-quota-head.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-curve-zoom-back.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-curve-selection.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-curve.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-name-wrap.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-window-rows.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/quota-count-wrap.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-card-refresh.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-focus-steady.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-all-accounts.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/usage-phone-head.test.cjs \
  internal/gui/tests/menu-first-second.test.cjs
```

### Tests that fail without the change

- Run the selection regression against original GUI assets: real assertion failure, legend button count **0 instead of 3**.
- Run the card-width regression against original GUI assets: real failure, **“default minimum is 360px, except a narrower container”**.
- Disable per-cycle coordinate mapping in temporary assets: the cycle-progress regression fails.
- Disable the single-entry hiding condition: the regression fails **“one available entry hides the control”**, `true` instead of `false`.

These checks failed through behavior assertions, not compilation or skipped tests. Temporary mutations were removed and the final regressions passed. Existing tests were updated for the new controls, plot-height measurement and explicitly compact packing fixtures. A separate test-only commit fixes a detached-tab race in focus-test setup while retaining every business assertion.

### Outstanding full Go suite

- `internal/agent`: `TestAlmaProvidersSeenDecodeOnce` reports 401 allocations. This single assertion was also independently reproduced on the original unchanged base. No claim is made that this permits shipping; no existing exact-name issue was found by the search.
- `internal/gateway`: `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON`, `TestMarshalSizedIsJSONMarshal` and `FuzzMarshalRaw/seed#7` fail byte/size parity with `encoding/json` for U+2028/U+2029 and invalid UTF-8. Related report: [#5348](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/5348).
- `internal/gateway`: `TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback` says the IPv6 address still answers after the WSL listener closes. [#3680](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3680) explains the probe's reused keep-alive connection and has [a proposed test patch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/1b93ee5c883344549c48ed1a152d5fe31f431b22). Its full discussion was read; the patch has not been reviewed or ported in this GUI changeset and remains work before merge.
- `internal/gui`: `TestLaneLimitRoutes` receives owner-lane data where it expects an empty object. [#5150](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/5150) explains that a temporary HOME does not isolate `gateway.OwnerLanes()` from its read-only GET to an already running gateway. The test does not need production fallback changed; its owner endpoint needs a controlled fixture. No account/lane payload is published here.

All linked issues and every current comment were read. The non-Alma failures were not independently rerun against this PR's unchanged base, so they are not all labeled baseline failures. No unrelated Go implementation or test assertion was changed to make this feature appear green.

### Outstanding i18n check

`a plugin's words are its own` reports:

- Library: `Use the library's` is also found in `internal/library/skills_shared_copy_test.go`.
- Routing: `No session ID` is also found in `internal/gui/trace.go`.
- Usage: `View routing` is also found in `internal/gui/search_row_archive_test.go`.

These same conflicts were independently reproduced on the original unchanged base. They are tracked in upstream issues [#5332](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/5332), [#5327](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/5327), [#5426](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/5426) and [#5482](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/5482); their bodies and every current comment were read. That reproduction does not waive the repository's merge criteria. No unrelated ownership changes are included here.

This remains a **draft**: full-suite failures, unrun GUI/native checks and maintainer approval of the layout/default change must be addressed before merge. A maintainer should recheck the accepted head merged onto current main as required by the code standards.

timeline.body:
Fixed on [fix/5348-json-runtime-parity](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5348-json-runtime-parity), commit [102f2b1d](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/102f2b1de6d718d62f0ae8fa53fd6ca469ecff50), based on upstream `ed0ab567`.

The fast encoder now derives the separator and invalid-UTF-8 replacement behavior once from the active `encoding/json` implementation. The string writer and size calculation use the same replacement bytes. HTML escaping remains separately controlled, and the existing fast path is retained. This avoids hard-coding Go 1.27 behavior into builds using the supported Go 1.26.8 runtime.

On the unchanged base, the two reported tests fail on Go 1.27.3 and pass on cached Go 1.26.8. After the patch, focused exact-byte and size parity tests pass on both. Independent review also ran all 29 existing fuzz seeds and a real Responses-to-Chat Handler test under race detection; nogui vet/build pass. Existing equality assertions were not relaxed.

No full repository suite, native macOS/Windows run or performance benchmark was performed. The linked fork PRs were checked: they cite these failures as pre-existing and do not change the encoder. AI-assisted implementation and independent review.
